hook_text: A supermarket advertised 40 posts. 3,000 applications arrived. Do that maths.
clip_script: When a new supermarket opened outside town, it advertised forty posts. By the closing date, more than three thousand applications had arrived. Three thousand. For forty. That means two thousand nine hundred and sixty letters of regret — most of them sent to people under thirty, holding certificates, who did everything they were told to do. Now walk across town: an engineering workshop has re-advertised the same artisan post three times, because nobody qualified has applied. Three thousand applications for shelf-packing; three for millwrighting. Same economy, opposite queues — and that contrast is the whole topic. Unemployment isn't one thing: the graduate waiting for a start date needs faster matching; the machinist whose plant relocated needs retraining, not another advert; the builder cut in a downturn comes back when the cranes do. Five different stories, five different fixes. And the people who stopped applying after a hundred silences? The official count loses them the day they stop. The queue you can see is long — the one you can't see is longer.
visual_style: A stack of CVs growing into a tower beside a tiny '40 posts' sign; a split screen of two queues — one stretching beyond the frame, one of three figures beside a ringing phone; five faces appearing with one-word labels as their stories are named; figures at the queue's end fading to outlines.
mood: Sober, respectful, precise — the dignity of the queue kept intact while the analysis lands.
pacing: Quiet arithmetic at the open, sharp pivot at the two-queues contrast, brisk through the five stories, hushed final beat on the uncounted.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to diagnose before prescribing.
